title: Live updates: Bitcoin holds near $82,000 as Nasdaq rebounds more than 1%
summary: Bitcoin treasury company Strive continued to add large numbers of BTC to its balance sheet, while far larger peer Strategy acquired only a small amount.
content:
coverage endedOct 19, 2026, 4:44 p.m. EDT

Bitcoin treasury company Strive continued to add large numbers of BTC to its balance sheet, while far larger peer Strategy acquired only a small amount.

Saylor responds to naysayers on STRC buybacks

Strategy Executive Chairman Michael Saylor is coming under some social media heat for the company’s continued buybacks of its high-yielding preferred stock STRC at just modest discounts to $100 par value.

The company this morning announced the repurchase of $193 million of STRC, bringing total buybacks to nearly $2 billion. Strategy also announced an increase in the authorized buyback amount to $3 billion from $2 billion.

Recall that the buyback program started this past summer following STRC plunging nearly all the way to $70, putting in question the future of the security. In recent weeks, though, STRC has traded mostly above $98, prompting some to wonder if Strategy’s money might not be better spent on buying more bitcoin at what may (or may not) be close to bear market lows, rather than repurchasing preferred stock trading at only a very minor discount.

And others are curious that the fast pace of buybacks (Strategy has less than $9 billion of STRC issued), combined with a 12% dividend yield, hasn’t been enough to fully return STRC to $100.

“You don’t build a market worth trillions without investing billions,” said Saylor on Monday, in response to some of that criticism.

STRC is higher by 1.3% on Monday to $98.99.

US midterm elections unlikely to drive crypto prices, Schwab says

The upcoming U.S. midterm elections may have less impact on crypto prices than investors expect, according to Jim Ferraioli, head of crypto research at the Schwab Center for Financial Research.

Schwab found little evidence that rising odds of Democrats taking control of Congress have consistently weighed on crypto returns, even when prediction market trading volumes were high.

While election headlines could trigger short-term volatility, Ferraioli said congressional control has explained little of crypto's recent price movements.

Bipartisan support for crypto legislation and the possibility of continued regulatory progress also suggest that a divided Congress would not necessarily hurt the market.

CoreWeave gives up gains, hits new 52week low

Troubled neocloud CoreWeave (CRWV) — despite a general risk-on attitude on Monday and an upgrade to buy at Goldman Sachs — has been unable to hold onto early gains.

The stock minutes ago sank below $60 to a new 52-week low after earlier rising to $66.

The Nasdaq remains higher by more than 1%.

Yields back on the rise as last week's market panic abates

A shaky start for U.S. stocks has resolved to the upside in late-morning trading, with the Nasdaq sitting at a session high, up 1.8%. The S&P 500 is also at its high for the day, up 0.9%.

Gains are being led by the roughed-up AI space, with defensive sectors like healthcare and consumer staples — which were positive last week — posting modest losses.

Despite two of the uglier inflation reports in recent memory, the U.S. bond market surged last week as the tumble in equities prompted investors to put money into “safe” fixed income.

The panic having subsided for the moment, interest rates are back on the rise. The U.S. 10-year Treasury yield is up 3.3 basis points to 5.133% after having nearly fallen through 5% at one point last week. Rate hike odds for next week’s Fed meeting have risen to 18% after having dropped to as low as 12% last week.

Bitcoin remains pinned near $82,000.

'Davos in the desert' faces questions after attacks in Saudi Arabia

Saudi Arabian organizers are mulling the postponement of the annual Future Investment Initiative — often dubbed “Davos in the desert” — after upped attacks against Saudi Arabia by Yemen’s Houthis, reported the FT.

Also under discussion, instead of postponement, would be holding the event virtually, the story added.

Among the scheduled speakers are BlackRock’s Larry Fink and JPMorgan’s Jamie Dimon.

The event is set to take place Oct. 26-29.

Homebuilder sentiment tumbles to weakest since 2012

Surging interest rates appear to be forcing another leg down in the housing industry.

The NAHB Housing Market Index for newly built homes fell to 29 this month from an already weak 32 in September. Economist forecasts had been for the gauge to remain steady at 32.

The NAHB is a diffusion index, meaning a reading above 50 suggests more confidence; below 50, the opposite.

Current sales conditions fell two points in October to 33. Sales expectations in the next six months slid five points to 32. Buyer traffic fell five points to 18.

The survey found 43% of builders cutting prices in October, the highest rate in the 2020-2026 period.

Bitcoin trading at $82,000 as stocks open with tenuous gains

Roughly 30 minutes into the U.S. trading day, tech stocks are bouncing from last week’s carnage, but the gains are a bit more modest than futures trading suggested.

The Nasdaq is ahead 0.85%, with roughed-up AI-related favorites like Micron, Intel, SanDisk, and AMD posting gains in the 4%-7% range.

The S&P 500 is higher by 0.4%, and the DJIA is down 0.25%.

After touching $83,000 overnight, bitcoin has drifted back down to $82,000, up 0.8% over the past 24 hours. Ether, solana, and XRP are also slightly higher.

Bitmine bought another $30 million in ether

Ethereum-focused treasury firm Bitmine BMNR$21.58·Market Closed is still adding to its crypto stash, buying another 12,535 ETH last week.

The haul is worth about $30.4 million at recent ETH prices, and it was almost identical to the previous week’s purchase.

The firm now holds 6.04 million ETH, leaving it roughly 64,000 tokens short of its goal of owning 5% of Ethereum's supply.

At that rate, Bitmine could hit its 5% target in about five weeks, assuming Ethereum's supply stays near current levels.

Chairman Tom Lee said earlier that the company plans to stop accumulating ETH once it reaches that target.

Metaplanet moves closer to U.S. bitcoin treasury platform as shareholders approve Superplanet deal

Super League shareholders have approved Metaplanet’s proposed takeover, according to Metaplanet CEO, Simon Gerovich, which paves the way for the companys rebrand to Superplanet (SUPA), a U.S.-listed bitcoin treasury platform.

At closing, Metaplanet will contribute 2,100 BTC out of its 44,000 BTC and $2.5 million for approximately 93.7% ownership, with its shares locked up for five years.

Superplanet plans to grow bitcoin per share primarily through non-convertible perpetual preferred stock, expanding Metaplanet’s access to U.S. capital markets.

Strategy purchased 267 bitcoin last week, while Strive added 1,223

Michael Saylor’s Strategy MSTR$135.98·Market Closed acquired a modest 267 bitcoin last week, bringing total holdings to 848,517 coins. The company also bought back another $193 million of its high-yielding preferred stock STRC and boosted the size of that repurchase program to $3 billion from $2 billion.

STRC fell back to $97.72 during last week’s market-wide selloff, likely indicating that Saylor and team will continue buying back shares rather than issuing them to acquire more bitcoin.

Matt Cole’s Strive ASST$25.56·Market Closed, meanwhile, continued its relatively fast bitcoin acquisition spree, adding another 1,223 coins and bringing total holdings to 36,818.

The company will have another $600 million in buying power later this week when the IPO proceeds from its SATA preferred stock offering hit its bank account.

Strive’s original high-yielding preferred stock SATA was also caught up in the market panic last week, falling all the way back to $96.83. It had previously spent several weeks trading at or above par value ($100), allowing the company to use it as a funding mechanism to buy more bitcoin.

Wall Street's fear index, VIX, drops 5%

Cboe’s VIX index, also known as Wall Street’s fear gauge, is down 5% as of this writing.

The index, representing the market’s expectations for the degree of price swings in the S&P 500 over the next four weeks, is hovering just below 19. It surged by over 20% to nearly 20 on Friday as AI stocks tanked.

Friday spikes in the VIX have historically eased by Monday.

French bond spread on the rise after weekend riots

The U.S. equity market appears poised for a strong rebound on Monday, and Treasury rates are slipping, but that’s not the case in Europe.

Leading a 1.3% decline in the Euro Stoxx 50 is France’s CAC 40, lower by 1.65% following ugly-looking rioting in that country over the weekend.

Bond yields are moving higher as well; the French 10-year OAT yield is up 11 basis points to 4.89%, while the German 10-year Bund yield gains just 3.5% basis points to 3.44%. That puts the 10-year spread between the two to 145 basis points, the highest level in two weeks.

Bitcoin’s weekend bounce is still just a rebound, FxPro says, as bulls lean on October seasonality

Dip buyers defended bitcoin’s 50-day moving average again over the weekend, lifting it 1.4% to about $82,800 on Monday, but FxPro’s chief market analyst Alex Kuptsikevich is calling it a rebound for now.

The 50-day moving average, bitcoin’s average closing price over the past 50 days, sits near $81,000 and has caught every dip since last Tuesday. Holding it keeps the medium-term trend intact. Breaking higher takes more than that.

“This rise is better described as a rebound than a resumption of upward momentum,” Kuptsikevich said in an email to CoinDesk.

He pointed to last summer as a guide, when bitcoin chopped around similar levels for more than a month back then, and only a sharp surge on Aug. 19 kicked off the rally that followed.

Bulls are leaning on the calendar. Traditional markets often put in a local bottom toward the end of October, Kuptsikevich said, and crypto investors are betting that pattern helps them claw back last week’s losses.

'Irrational despair': Neolcouds rising early Monday after last week's plunge

“Irrational despair,” goes the title of a note from StoneX’s Mark Palmer on Galaxy Digital GLXY$15.71·Market Closed, one of the names swept up in the panic over AI data center stocks over the past couple of weeks.

The market is valuing GLXY as if CoreWeave (CRWV) — Galaxy’s tenant at its Helios data center — has already failed and Galaxy could find no other tenants, argued Palmer.

He reiterated his buy rating and $57 price target on GLXY. GLXY is higher by 3% pre-market to $16.80 following last week’s 20% decline.

Goldman Sachs is boosting the mood as well, upgrading CoreWeave to buy from neutral.

CRWV is up 6% after falling 23.5%. Hut 8 HUT$68.12·Market Closed, TeraWulf WULF$12.05·Market Closed and IREN IREN$27.73·Market Closed are among those rising more than 5%.

Elon Musk to give away SpaceX shares to American children

“Next year, I will give one of my SpaceX SPCX$147.99·Market Closed shares to every kid in America,” tweeted Elon Musk early Monday morning. “This will be the first of many.”

The company reports its third-quarter results after the close on Thursday.

Oil reverses early drop as U.S. issues security alerts across Middle East nations

Oil prices have bounced from Asian session lows on fears of a fresh escalation in Middle East geopolitical tensions.

WTI futures have recovered to $98.55, down just 0.5% on the day, after hitting a low of $96.72 during Asian hours. Bitcoin BTC$81,666.57 and ether ETH$2,395.46 have erased their early gains.

A few hours ago, the U.S. reportedly issued warnings across 12 locations in the Middle East, warning it citizens of potential flight cancellations and airspace closures. The warning covers Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates (UAE), Kuwait, Jordan, Bahrain, Oman, Iran, Qatar, Iraq, Lebanon, Yemen and Israel/Jerusalem.

This has triggered fears of fresh U.S. strikes on Iran and continued disruption of oil flow through the pivotal Strait of Hormuz.

Bitcoin pokes above $83,000 for a moment as tech futures snap a weeklong skid

Bitcoin climbed from an overnight low near $80,700 to just above $83,000 early Monday, then slipped back to about $82,400 within half an hour. Sellers were waiting for the move.

It was a quick turn. Bitcoin is up 0.3% over 24 hours, and $83,000 is still about $1,000 short of the ceiling that turned it back twice last week, near $84,000 on Oct. 13 and again on Oct. 14.

The bounce tracked a rebound in tech. Nasdaq 100 futures climbed 1.1%, snapping a weeklong 5.5% selloff, and S&P 500 futures rose 0.5%. An ETF tracking chipmakers jumped 3% before the U.S. open, on course for its first gain in 10 sessions. This week’s earnings will put the AI trade under the spotlight again.

Europe was weaker. The Stoxx 600 fell 0.8% after a weekend of protests in France, French bonds led a selloff in European debt, and the euro was the worst performer among major currencies. The dollar was flat, and Brent crude slipped from a five-month high.

A move through $84,000 would be the first sign the tech rebound is pulling bitcoin up with it.

title: Dogecoin (DOGE) Price Prediction: Whales Add 600M DOGE as Bulls Defend $0.08 Support
summary: Dogecoin (DOGE) price prediction examines $0.08 support as whales add 600M tokens, spot outflows hit $58.7M, and traders watch for a recovery toward $0.10.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: DOGE

Dogecoin (DOGE) price prediction examines $0.08 support as whales add 600M tokens, spot outflows hit $58.7M, and traders watch for a recovery toward $0.10.

Dogecoin is trying to stabilize near $0.08 after another weak session, leaving the market caught between improving whale activity and continued selling pressure in the spot market. According to Brave New Coin, DOGE is trading around $0.07845, down 2.45% over the past 24 hours

Dogecoin Breakout Holds but Momentum Remains Weak

Dogecoin has already pushed through the long-running descending trendline, removing one of the main technical barriers that had capped price since the 2024 peak. The breakout is therefore in effect, but the follow-through has been underwhelming. DOGE remains trapped inside the broader accumulation zone around $0.07-$0.10 instead of expanding cleanly higher.

Dogecoin breaks its long-term downtrend but remains below $0.10 resistance. Source: TehLamboXcharts via X

That lack of momentum is important. TehLamboXcharts weekly chart shows price repeatedly holding the lower part of the range, but buyers have not yet generated enough strength to move decisively through the upper boundary near $0.10. Until that happens, the trendline breakout remains constructive without becoming a confirmed expansion from the base.

The next meaningful confirmation would come from DOGE price establishing itself above the accumulation range and pushing toward $0.11985. A move through that level would give the breakout considerably more weight and begin opening the larger recovery structure towards $0.30603. For now, however, price is still proving whether the recent trendline break can develop into something more than a temporary structural improvement.

The $0.07-$0.08 region remains the area bulls need to defend while momentum rebuilds. Holding the base would keep the breakout intact and leave $0.11985 as the next important upside level, while a sustained loss of the accumulation zone would weaken the setup despite the earlier trendline break.

Whale Demand Builds Despite Spot Outflows

Dogecoin’s latest positioning data is beginning to show a clear split between larger holders and the broader spot market. Santiment figures shared by Ali Charts show whale balances rising from around 55.60 billion DOGE to 56.21 billion between October 12 and October 16, an increase of roughly 600 million tokens while price remains close to the $0.08 region.

Dogecoin whales add roughly 600 million DOGE near $0.08 support. Source: Ali Charts via X

That accumulation gives the current support zone more weight. Whales are increasing exposure during weakness rather than chasing price higher, suggesting that larger holders are showing greater confidence around the lower end of the range. If DOGE continues to hold near $0.078-$0.08, that demand could help support another attempt toward $0.09-$0.10.

The spot market is sending a different message. Data shared by CW8900 shows roughly $58.73 million in net outflows over the latest 24-hour period, while one-week outflows stand near $92.24 million and the 30-day figure has reached approximately $208.56 million. That means broader selling pressure is still present even as whale balances move higher.

Dogecoin records $58.73 million in spot net outflows over 24 hours. Source: CW8900 via X

For now, the divergence between whale demand and spot outflows keeps the setup balanced. A reduction in selling pressure, combined with continued accumulation around $0.08, would strengthen the recovery case considerably.

Bearish View: DOGE Risks a Move Toward $0.066

DOGE still carries a clear downside risk if the current $0.078-$0.08 support area gives way. The liquidation heatmap shows a sizeable concentration of liquidity sitting lower around $0.066-$0.068, which could become increasingly relevant if sellers regain control.

That lower pocket matters because price often gravitates toward areas where liquidity remains exposed, particularly when nearby support starts to weaken. With spot outflows still elevated, a sustained break below $0.078 would make the $0.066 region a more realistic downside objective rather than just a distant technical level.

Dogecoin’s liquidation heatmap highlights downside liquidity near 0.066–0.068. Source: CAGThe3rd via X

The heatmap also shows liquidity above price near $0.093-$0.10, but the bearish case remains active while DOGE price struggles to build momentum from current support. A stronger recovery through $0.084-$0.09 would begin to reduce that risk, while continued weakness would leave the lower liquidity zone vulnerable to a sweep.

Dogecoin Short to Medium-Term Outlook

Dogecoin’s short- to medium-term outlook is still mixed, but the balance is beginning to improve around the $0.078-$0.08 region. The weekly trendline breakout remains intact, whales have added roughly 600 million DOGE price near support, and price continues to hold inside the broader accumulation range. Against that, spot outflows remain heavy, and the lower $0.066-$0.068 liquidity pocket is still exposed if current support gives way.

The more constructive signal is coming from momentum. Sweep’s chart shows a confirmed bullish divergence, with price making lower lows while RSI forms higher lows. That kind of divergence often appears when downside momentum is starting to weaken, and in DOGE’s case it is developing directly around a support area that has already attracted repeated buyer interest.

The divergence becomes more important if price begins to follow through. A recovery through roughly $0.084-$0.086 would be the first sign that momentum is shifting back towards buyers, while a move above $0.09-$0.093 would strengthen the case that the current base is turning into a broader recovery rather than another temporary bounce.

Dogecoin shows bullish RSI divergence near $0.08 support as buyers seek a recovery. Source: Sweep via X

From there, $0.10 becomes the key short-term breakout level. Clearing it would show that DOGE is finally escaping the accumulation range and would bring $0.11985 back into focus. If the bullish divergence fails to produce that follow-through and $0.078 breaks instead, the setup would weaken quickly, and the $0.066-$0.068 liquidity zone would become the more relevant downside target.

Final Thoughts: Dogecoin Price Prediction for Q4 2026

Dogecoin has already shown a glimpse of what a stronger Q4 could look like. The September push higher came with improving volume and briefly lifted DOGE toward the $0.09-$0.10 area before price pulled back. The current move is now acting more like a retest of that breakout attempt than a completely new setup, which puts greater emphasis on how price behaves around the $0.078-$0.08 support zone.

Dogecoin was trading at around $0.0784, down 2.45% in the last 24 hours at press time. Source: Brave New Coin

For the broader Dogecoin Price Prediction, holding $0.078-$0.08 keeps the Q4 setup constructive and leaves $0.10-$0.11985 as the first recovery zone. A stronger breakout could then open at $0.25, with $0.40 becoming the larger higher-timeframe target if momentum continues.

title: XRP Price Prediction: Elliott Wave Setup and Descending Trendline Breakout Offer Hope as XRP Tests $1.30
summary: XRP is testing a critical technical zone near $1.30 as traders watch for a descending trendline breakout and confirmation of a potential Elliott Wave recovery.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: XRP

XRP is testing a critical technical zone near $1.30 as traders watch for a descending trendline breakout and confirmation of a potential Elliott Wave recovery.

However, resistance and weakening order-book demand continue to complicate XRP’s near-term outlook.

The current price forecast hinges on whether buyers can reclaim $1.31 and sustain upward momentum. A successful move could open the way toward $1.35, while a breakdown below nearby support would bring lower Fibonacci retracement levels into focus.

XRP Price Tests $1.31 as Buyers Attempt a Trendline Breakout

XRP’s latest price action reflects a market searching for direction after a sustained October pullback. Historical data from CoinGecko shows the token closing at $1.29 on October 17, down from $1.41 on October 11. The decline followed a rejection near $1.50 earlier in the month.

XRP failed to hold $1.31 resistance on October 16 but rebounded from a $1.29 wick on overnight buying. Source: @MarzellCrypto via X

The recovery attempt remains limited. Crypto analyst @MarzellCrypto highlighted XRP’s failure to maintain a position above $1.31 on October 16. The four-hour chart showed the price briefly falling toward $1.29 before overnight buying helped it recover.

The analyst identified $1.31 as the immediate level buyers need to reclaim. A sustained move above this threshold could put $1.35 in focus, while a break below $1.29 would expose the deeper support near $1.284.

As of October 19, XRP was trading around $1.31, according to historical market data. 

This places the cryptocurrency close to the resistance level identified in the short-term analysis, but the proximity alone does not confirm a breakout.

The current setup resembles earlier periods of consolidation in which XRP struggled to establish support after a decline. In a previous XRP price analysis published by Brave New Coin, analysts also identified the $1.30 area as an important level to monitor following rejection from higher resistance.

Elliott Wave Analysis Highlights $1.21–$1.30 Support

A separate technical assessment from crypto analyst @Morecryptoonl focuses on the possibility of a descending trendline breakout. The analyst shared a one-hour XRP/USD chart from MCO Global Research featuring an Elliott Wave structure, with numbered waves and an ABC corrective pattern.

Elliott Wave analysis suggests XRP needs a strong bullish reaction at current support to confirm the 1-2 setup and potential upward impulse. Source: @Morecryptoonl via X

The chart shows XRP testing a downward-sloping resistance line while trading near $1.30. Such a breakout could indicate that selling pressure is easing, but confirmation would require a sustained move above the trendline rather than a brief intraday push.

The analysis also identifies several Fibonacci retracement levels that could influence the next move:

  • $1.293: The 50% retracement level, close to the recent trading range.
  • $1.212: The 61.8% retracement level, which could become relevant if near-term support fails.
  • $1.106: The 78.6% retracement level, representing a deeper downside reference.

These levels provide potential areas of support rather than guaranteed price floors. Their significance depends on XRP’s reaction as the price approaches each zone.

In a separate daily-chart analysis, @Morecryptoonl argued that XRP needs a clear bullish reaction from its current support area to validate a potential Elliott Wave 1–2 setup. Under this interpretation, the recent decline could represent a corrective phase before another upward impulse.

However, Elliott Wave analysis is interpretive. Different analysts can assign different wave counts to the same price structure, and the proposed recovery remains unconfirmed until price action supports it.

A sustained hold above the $1.29–$1.30 region would strengthen the immediate stabilization case. Conversely, a decisive break below this zone could shift attention toward $1.21 before the lower $1.106 Fibonacci level comes into consideration.

XRP Faces Overhead Selling Pressure as Order-Book Demand Weakens

While the trendline and Elliott Wave setups offer a potential recovery scenario, order-book conditions present another obstacle.

Crypto analyst @Xaif_Crypto highlighted sell orders concentrated above XRP’s current price near $1.30, alongside thinning buy orders below the market. The analysis suggests that buyers may struggle to push the price higher if available demand cannot absorb the selling pressure.

XRP faces heavy sell walls near $1.30 and weakening bids below, raising the risk of a drop toward $1.20 support without stronger buying pressure. Source: @Xaif_Crypto via X

Order-book liquidity represents the limit orders available to buy or sell an asset at different prices. A concentration of sell orders can create short-term resistance, although these orders may be canceled or changed before execution. It is therefore not a reliable standalone indicator of future price direction.

According to @Xaif_Crypto’s assessment, weakening buying pressure could expose XRP to a retest of $1.20 support. That level also sits close to the $1.212 Fibonacci retracement identified in the Elliott Wave analysis, making the area relevant across both technical approaches.

The analyst has also expressed a longer-term bullish view, comparing XRP’s potential to Google’s early development in 2003 and pointing to possible institutional adoption. However, that comparison represents an investment thesis rather than evidence that XRP will follow a similar growth trajectory.

For the immediate XRP price prediction, the distinction between short-term trading pressure and longer-term expectations is important. Institutional adoption may influence demand over time, but it does not remove the near-term risks created by resistance, declining momentum, or insufficient buying liquidity.

Macro Outlook and Bitcoin Could Influence XRP’s Next Move

XRP’s technical structure is only one factor shaping its near-term outlook. Broader cryptocurrency market conditions, particularly Bitcoin’s direction, could also affect whether the token maintains its current support.

XRP faces strong resistance at $1.50–$1.60 and the descending 50-week EMA, with repeated rejections signaling near-term caution. Source: ChartNerdTA via X

ChartNerdTA has identified resistance between $1.50 and $1.60, where the price has struggled alongside the descending 50-week exponential moving average (EMA). The analyst also warned that a close below the 20-week EMA near $1.34 could increase the risk of a deeper retracement toward $1.00–$1.10.

The analysis identifies Bitcoin falling below $83,000 as another potential source of downside pressure. A decline in the largest cryptocurrency can weaken sentiment across the broader market, although XRP does not necessarily follow Bitcoin’s movements at the same pace or magnitude.

The lower support range could eventually develop into a double-bottom formation if XRP revisits the area around $1.00–$1.10 and subsequently rebounds. Such a pattern requires two distinct lows near a similar price level, separated by a recovery. It cannot be confirmed simply because the price approaches a previous low.

This scenario is consistent with the broader support-and-resistance framework discussed in Brave New Coin’s earlier XRP analysis, which examined the importance of reclaiming resistance before a sustained recovery could develop.

For now, the macro picture remains conditional. Bitcoin’s direction, broader risk appetite, and the response to XRP’s nearby technical levels will help determine whether buyers can establish a more durable recovery.

XRP Price Prediction: $1.35 Upside or $1.20 Downside?

The immediate XRP price forecast depends on how the market responds around $1.29–$1.31. The descending trendline breakout attempt and Elliott Wave structure provide a potential recovery framework, but neither has yet established a confirmed bullish reversal.

title: Bitcoin extends bounce above $82,000 as stocks rebound, DeFi tokens lead altcoin gains
summary: Bitcoin rose 0.8% to around $82,700 as China’s GDP beat estimates and Nasdaq futures rebounded, while the CoinDesk 80 gained 1.3% and DeFi led gains.
content:
Oct 19, 2026, 6:26 a.m. EDT

3 min read

Summary

  • Bitcoin traded around $82,500, up about 0.4% since midnight UTC, extending a rebound from Sunday’s dip to roughly $80,700.
  • The CoinDesk 80 gained 0.9%, triple the CoinDesk 5’s 0.e5% rise, with all six members of the DeFi index higher and arbitrum adding 6.7%.
  • Nasdaq 100 futures rose more than 1% and Asian stocks advanced after China’s third-quarter GDP growth beat expectations and oil prices eased.

Bitcoin BTC$81,637.45 is trading around $82,500, up around 0.5% since midnight UTC, extending a bounce from Sunday’s dip to roughly $80,700 and comfortably above Thursday’s brief break below $80,000.

Altcoins outpaced the largest cryptocurrency, with ether ETH$2,395.23 adding 0.75% to near $2,430 and the CoinDesk 80 (CD80) gaining 0.9%, triple the 0.35% rise in the bitcoin-heavy CoinDesk 5 (CD5). DeFi led the CoinDesk benchmarks with a 0.81% gain, with all six members of the DFX sector index higher.

The rebound follows a rough week for U.S. tech. The Nasdaq fell 4.5% in its worst weekly decline since June as worries over AI spending and debt hit stocks such as CoreWeave (CRWV), which fell 25%. On Monday, Nasdaq 100 futures advanced more than 1% alongside gains in Asian stocks after China’s third-quarter GDP growth of 4.5% beat expectations and oil prices eased, with earnings from Meta Platforms META$705.32·Market Closed and Tesla TSLA$368.04·Market Closed due this week.

Derivatives positioning

  • Volume jumps, positioning doesn't: Total 24-hour crypto futures volume rose 51% to $146 billion, while open interest (OI) edged up just 1.25% to $141 billion as traders churned through more contracts without adding much net exposure. Liquidations were $329 million, little changed from a day earlier, and the taker long-short volume ratio is balanced, so neither side is forcing the other out.
  • Majors rally with more leverage than spot buying: BTC, ETH, SOL and XRP all gained, and their notional OI grew faster than their prices in a sign that fresh capital is entering the contracts. Annualized perpetual funding is positive on all four, so longs are paying to hold. The 24-hour OI-adjusted cumulative volume delta (CVD) is flat to negative, though, meaning aggressive selling at least matched aggressive buying. The gains look position-led, and that makes them more fragile.
  • DOGE, UNI and crude oil perps see positions unwind: OI fell in all three despite flat-to-negative price action. Traders are closing positions and pulling capital out, not adding to bets on the downside.
  • ADA's bounce meets bearish positioning: ADA rose almost 1% in 24 hours, yet its annualized perp funding is -8%, the only negative print among the majors. Shorts are paying to stay short, and CVD is negative too. If the bounce continues, that crowded short side could become a source of buying.
  • Crypto volatility gauges stay calm as the VIX spikes: Bitcoin's and ether's 30-day implied volatility indexes, BVIV and EVIV, still signal calm, even as Wall Street's equivalent, VIX, surged on Friday. VIX history points to a likely normalization on Monday.
  • Bitcoin put-buyers dominate Deribit: The five most traded options on Deribit over the past 24 hours were all bitcoin puts at strikes below the current market price. Traders use puts to hedge long exposure against spot declines, so some are insuring gains. Ether flows look mixed.

Token talk

  • Arbitrum ARB$0.2001, an Ethereum layer-2 token, rose 6.7% to about $0.20, with the rally stemming from the Arbitrum Foundation’s Stablecoin Growth Program, announced on Thursday. The program sets aside 2 million ARB for the first 10 teams to hold $10 million in USDG, a dollar-pegged stablecoin issued by Paxos Digital Singapore. ARB has risen by 16.45% since the announcement.
  • Pump.fun PUMP$0.004395, the token of the Solana memecoin launchpad, jumped 7.6%, recouping part of a weekend slide that took it to about $0.0039 on Sunday. While there was no news catalyst for the move, 24-hour trading volume doubled to $215 million.
  • DeFi tokens advanced across the board, with uniswap (UNI) up 3.2% to around $7.42, while lido LDO$0.3964 and ethena (ENA) rose by 2.5% and 1.6% respectively as the sector recovers from last month’s Clarity Act delay and shrinking yields.
  • Celestia (TIA) gave back 3.9% to about 61 cents after Friday’s 16% jump, while starknet STRK$0.05708 slipped 1.0% to 6 cents. STRK’s market value has fallen about a quarter since Friday morning, according to CoinDesk data.
  • The larger cryptocurrencies were mostly higher, with solana (SOL) rising 1.6% to about $106, XRP gaining 0.6% and BNB adding 0.36%. Cardano ADA$0.2172 slipped 0.15% and hedera HBAR$0.08288 fell 0.83%.
  • The “Altcoin Season” index is at 56/100, tumbling from last week’s high of 63/100, the 2026 record.

title: JPMorgan brings JPM Coin, representing dollar deposits, to Ethereum
summary: JPMorgan's dollar deposit token is heading to Ethereum as the lender looks to offer it to wider selection of institutional clients.
content:
Updated Oct 19, 2026, 10:06 a.m. EDTPublished Oct 19, 2026, 6:03 a.m. EDT

2 min read

Summary

  • JPMorgan made JPM Coin, a token representing dollar deposits at the bank, available to institutional clients on Ethereum.
  • Ethereum’s liquidity makes it attractive for crypto companies seeking blockchain payments and financial firms settling trades or backing tokenized assets, the bank told Bloomberg.
  • The move expands JPMorgan’s blockchain efforts beyond its private Kinexys network, which processes more than $7 billion in transactions daily, and the Ethereum layer-2 network, Base.

JPMorgan(JPM), the largest U.S. bank, brought its almost year-old crypto token, JPM Coin, to Ethereum as part of a plan to expand beyond Base, the layer-2 blockchain built by Coinbase Global COIN$168.31·Market Closed.

JPM Coin, which represents dollar deposits at the bank, was technically deployed on the Ethereum mainnet on Monday and is available for institutional clients’ use, the bank said in an emailed statement.

The bank chose Ethereum because the blockchain offers more liquidity than rival networks and is already used by institutional clients, Emma Landriault, the head of Kinexys Labs at JPMorgan’s blockchain division Kinexys, said in an interview with Bloomberg, which reported the news earlier.

“Issuing JPM Coin first on Base and now on Ethereum is a meaningful step towards providing our institutional clients with multi-chain optionality for moving wholesale money across both the web3 and traditional finance ecosystems,” she said in the emailed statement.

The banking giant flagged a move outside Base back in January, saying it was planning to take the token to the Canton Network. Broadening its availability aims to serve crypto firms that want to make blockchain payments and financial firms that need a digital token to settle trades or back tokenized assets, Landriault said.

Tokenization is the process of converting real-world assets and financial assets into a digital form that’s recorded and traded on a decentralized ledger. The advantage is speed, including faster settlement of trades, quick movement of money while bypassing delays and frictions involved in traditional rails.

Banks have embraced tokenization, but mostly away from public networks. In the U.S., JPMorgan, Citi (C), Bank of America (BAC) and Wells Fargo (WFC), along with more than a dozen other banks, have plans to start a shared network for tokenized deposits.

JPMorgan’s private blockchain network, Kinexys, already handles more than $7 billion a day, a small piece in the bank’s $12 trillion a day payments business. Almost $50 billion worth of crypto assets are locked in Ethereum-based applications, according to DeFiLlama.

Abroad, JPMorgan is among more than 30 banks that are helping Swift, the interbank messaging service, define the features and governance of its blockchain-based ledger. In July, Swift said 17 banks, including Citi and Wells Fargo, were preparing to pilot live transactions on it. JPMorgan wasn’t on that list.

title: Bitwise Launches First U.S. Spot NEAR ETF With 5% Staking Rewards and $32B Intents
summary:
Key Takeaways: Bitwise’s NEAR ETF (NRR) is now available on NYSE Arca. The fund will stake NEAR with a maximum staking reward of approximately 5% per annum. Over $32 billion
The post Bitwise Launches First U.S. Spot NEAR ETF With 5% Staking Rewards and $32B Intents appeared first on CryptoNinjas.
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Bitwise’s NEAR ETF (NRR) is now available on NYSE Arca.
  • The fund will stake NEAR with a maximum staking reward of approximately 5% per annum.
  • Over $32 billion volume has been processed by NEAR Intents.

Bitwise Asset Management has launched the first U.S. spot exchange-traded product offering direct exposure to NEAR, giving traditional investors a new route into the blockchain’s token through brokerage accounts.

The Bitwise NEAR ETF debuted on NYSE Arca on September 29th under the symbol NRR, charging a 0.75% management fee, and offering a combination of the spot NEAR exposure and staking.

  • Bitwise Brings Spot NEAR Exposure to U.S. Investors
  • Staking Adds a 5% Yield Component
    • NEAR Intents Tops $32B in Transaction Volume
    • NRR Extends Bitwise’s NEAR Strategy Into the U.S.

Bitwise Brings Spot NEAR Exposure to U.S. Investors

NRR does not trade futures or other derivatives of NRR, but rather holds NRR outright. The structure can also cause the investors to demand ETF shares, which in turn could drive purchases of the underlying token to the ETF during its creation, potentially linking capital inflows to demand for the NEAR spot market.

The product offers investors a way to buy NEAR without having to deal directly with private keys and wallets, or go through a crypto exchange.

This family of single-asset crypto offerings has grown to now include Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP and Hyperliquid, the company said in a Monday release.

Read More: Bitwise Launches First Lighter ETP With 0.85% Fee, Bringing LIT to European Markets

Staking Adds a 5% Yield Component

Bitwise also plans to institutionalize a significant percentage of NRR’s holdings in NEAR.

The annualized neargstake reward rate was approximately 5 percent as of September 25, but this will not be a guaranteed rate of return. Net asset value will accrue the rewards a stakeholder earns from the fund, not as a fixed yield.

The structure brings in more risks, like the potential for slashing, operational challenges and liquidity problems from not having the tokens available at redemption time.

Read More: Bitwise Hyperliquid ETF Targets $11B HYPE Market

NEAR Intents Tops $32B in Transaction Volume

Bitwise is also marking the ETF release with the progress of NEAR’s position in the ecosystem of AI-powered blockchain infrastructure. According to data from Bitwise, NEAR Intents, the network’s cross-chain transaction protocol, has seen over $32 billion in transaction volume, down from under $1 billion a year ago.

The protocol’s goal was to enable users and autonomous software agents to interact in a distributed manner without needing to take care of each routing transaction individually.

Bitwise says this may grow even more important as AI agents start making payments, swaps and other financial transactions for users. NEAR transactions now complete in about 1.2 seconds, and Bitwise reported 100% uptime across the network for six years at this point.

NRR Extends Bitwise’s NEAR Strategy Into the U.S.

The U.S. opening follows Bitwise’s existing operation in Europe and already has a BaFin-approved staking ETP. As per the data as of June 30, 2026, Bitwise has managed around $9 billion worth of clients’ assets.

title: Binance Pay Opens Crypto Payments at Millions of PayPay Merchants Across Japan
summary:
Key Takeaways: Binance Pay is now available for visitors to use at PayPay merchants in Japan. Crypto is immediately converted to JPY. The Binance Pay tourist users have increased by
The post Binance Pay Opens Crypto Payments at Millions of PayPay Merchants Across Japan appeared first on CryptoNinjas...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Binance Pay is now available for visitors to use at PayPay merchants in Japan.
  • Crypto is immediately converted to JPY.
  • The Binance Pay tourist users have increased by 20% between July and August 2026.

Binance is expanding crypto payments in Japan through a new integration between Binance Pay and PayPay, one of the country’s largest QR payment networks.

It provides features which allow eligible tourists to use the crypto payments at the millions of stores supported by PayPay without a prior exchange of yen or sign up for a local payment account.

  • Binance Pay Connects Crypto to Japan’s PayPay Network
  • Stablecoins and Major Crypto Assets Can Fund Payments
    • Binance Pay Tourist Activity Jumps 20%
    • Japan Expands Binance Pay’s Asian QR Footprint

Binance Pay Connects Crypto to Japan’s PayPay Network

Japan is also allowing tourists to pay using crypto in the local retail market while they are travelling the country using their Binance account balance.

A merchant can have a code to open Binance Pay at checkout, and paykey can read the code to complete the transaction. For some stores, visitors can also scan the store’s PayPay QR and type the amount of the purchase.

The crypto currency is converted in real time to the JPY units and the merchant gets the local currency. That’s no longer a problem because travelers can use digital assets without having to sell them for JPY first or withdraw cash.

The feature is accessible just for tourists to Japan who are Binance ID verified customers. Not usable to Japanese people.

Read More: Binance Bitcoin Outflows Hit 13,800 BTC in 3-Year Record as FOMO Returns

Stablecoins and Major Crypto Assets Can Fund Payments

According to Binance’s description of its QR payment network, Binance Pay currently lets people pay for travel with assets like USDT, USDC, BTC, BNB and ETH.

The payment system will also perform the translation from crypto to fiat with checkout, so that all users still have the same purchasing process in every country.

Additionally, Binance claims that users are not charged any blockchain gas fees when making these payments via Binance Pay.

The solution simplifies the solution for travellers who would otherwise need to spend local currency first or make a separate wallet beforehand to send and receive crypto during travel.

Binance Pay Tourist Activity Jumps 20%

Binance has noted that there is an increasing trend of tourists using cryptocurrencies, with active users rising 20% from July to August 2026.

Japan becomes another market where the firm is expanding its payments with QR code business across Asia.

Instead of creating a new merchant network, Binance Pay integrates with the local payment ecosystem, allowing merchants to seamlessly utilize the QR codes already in use at their physical locations.

The same idea has been used in Vietnam as well, by integrating VietQR for tourists to pay with crypto while local fiat is paid to merchants.

Read More: Binance Wallet Opens $4.7T Pre-IPO Market Access Through PancakeSwap Tokenized Deals

Japan Expands Binance Pay’s Asian QR Footprint

PayPay provides Binance Pay with a vast network of merchants in convenient stores, restaurants and other common venues spread throughout Japan.

The integration is for bitcoin customers to spend cryptocurrencies the same way they spend money, rather than via a whole separate blockchain payment. Binance will roll out this model to other Asia-Pacific and other markets where QR payment is already popular.

The company is focusing on markets with strong tourist traffic and established QR infrastructure, allowing travelers to use one Binance Pay account across multiple destinations without changing their payment setup each time.

title: Morgan Stanley Builds Crypto Lab to Test Stablecoins, Tokenization and DeFi at Scale
summary:
Key Takeaways: Morgan Stanley has opened a Digital Asset Lab dedicated to blockchain technologies. The test is to be applied to the stablecoins, the tokenized assets and DeFi applications. This
The post Morgan Stanley Builds Crypto Lab to Test Stablecoins, Tokenization and DeFi at Scale appeared fir...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Morgan Stanley has opened a Digital Asset Lab dedicated to blockchain technologies.
  • The test is to be applied to the stablecoins, the tokenized assets and DeFi applications.
  • This lab allows employees to try things that they don’t want to do to the bank’s core systems.

Morgan Stanley has given its crypto research a boost with a new blockchain lab, dedicated to joining blockchain-based infrastructure into its financial business toolkit.

The initiative gives the Wall Street bank a controlled environment to study digital money, tokenized products and decentralized finance tools before considering wider deployment.

  • Morgan Stanley Tests Stablecoins and Tokenized Finance
  • DeFi Vaults Join the Testing List
    • Crypto Research Builds on Existing Products
    • Wall Street Pushes Deeper Into Blockchain Infrastructure

Morgan Stanley Tests Stablecoins and Tokenized Finance

The new lab will focus on blockchain based financial infrastructure and stablecoins, tokenized deposits, central bank digital currencies and tokenized money-market funds.

Morgan Stanley is also looking at deFi apps that might find their way into automating financial activity outside normal market hours.

A specific area of interest is how software-based systems can continuously handle investment strategies, with transactions recorded on the blockchain and investment rules executed as they are generated.

The lab will be part of Morgan Stanley’s existing innovation labs. Staff have the opportunity to trial new technology in a testing environment, minimising the impact on the bank’s primary systems.

Read More: South Korea Targets 2027 Tokenized Securities Launch with Stablecoin Settlement Vision

DeFi Vaults Join the Testing List

Another technology that is being considered is DeFi vaults. A smart contract could automate investment strategies or asset management functions as per programmed conditions within these systems. Morgan Stanley is investigating the possibility of combining the model with the standard available financial products.

The bank also plans to examine the differences between tokenized bank deposits and stablecoins. Unlike stablecoins which are backed by a different reserve asset, tokenized deposits are a claim against money that is held by a bank.

It is hoped that learning how both models can fit within institutional finance will be an integral aspect of the lab’s tasks.

Crypto Research Builds on Existing Products

Morgan Stanley is not entering digital assets from scratch. It already hosts Bitcoin, Ether and Solana on its E*TRADE platform for eligible clients and has also introduced cryptocurrency-based investment products.

The bank took the stablecoin industry in its stride too. The Morgan Stanley Investment Management government money-market portfolio was launched partly for the purpose of using it to hold a reserve of stablecoins.

That product focuses on reserve assets such as cash, short-term U.S. Treasurys and Treasury-backed repurchase agreements.

The new Digital Asset Lab is for a different purpose. It’s not another product on the market, It’s a test about how blockchain can be applied to financial operations.

Read More: Cloudflare Unveils Stablecoin Monetization Gateway, Unlocking Instant x402 Payments for Any API

Wall Street Pushes Deeper Into Blockchain Infrastructure

As major financial institutions show increased interest in tokenization of assets and blockchain settlement systems, Morgan Stanley’s research echoes the trend.

The bank is also exploring the banks of digital finance, from the underlying infrastructure of the system, like blockchain-based programmable assets and automated investment services, to custody.

For its part, the financial firm’s proposed trust platform is said to be part of Morgan Stanley’s plans to launch a crypto infrastructure, including custody and services provided by outside parties.

For now, the technologies being tested in the Digital Asset Lab remain experimental. Products such as tokenized deposits and DeFi vaults are research areas rather than services currently available to Morgan Stanley clients.

title: Trezor Cuts Resellers After $86M Wallet Tampering Scare, Says Devices Remain Safe
summary:
Key Takeaways: Trezor recently has seen hardware wallet supply chain issues, so it has shortened its list of authorized retailers. According to the company, no proof of any trespass on
The post Trezor Cuts Resellers After $86M Wallet Tampering Scare, Says Devices Remain Safe appeared first on Crypto...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Trezor recently has seen hardware wallet supply chain issues, so it has shortened its list of authorized retailers.
  • According to the company, no proof of any trespass on any Trezor devices.
  • This stems from a recent news report on malicious hardware implants being discovered in Ledger hardware from a reseller.

Trezor is bolstering its supply chain of hardware wallets, reducing the number of resellers authorized to distribute them. The company said that it is making the decision in anticipation of a breach and not as a result of a confirmed breach of any Trezor product.

Following recent supply-chain incidents, we decided to reduce the number of resellers so we can more effectively check those we work with.

Let us be very clear: there is not a single piece of evidence that Trezor devices have been compromised.

This is a preventive step, taken out of an abundance of caution. We also want to thank everyone involved for the cooperation, and for the years of work putting Trezor in people’s hands.

— Trezor (@Trezor) October 13, 2026

  • Trezor Reduces Reseller Network After Supply-Chain Incidents
  • Trezor Says No Devices Have Been Compromised
    • Hardware Wallet Security Moves Beyond Firmware
    • Users Urged to Check Where Their Wallet Comes From

Trezor Reduces Reseller Network After Supply-Chain Incidents

Trezor says it will engage fewer resellers, in an effort to more closely monitor the partners it is putting its hardware wallet products into the hands of. The firm attributed the action to counter security breaches in the hardware wallet space in the recent past.

Trezor CCO Danny Sanders also announced that some resellers had been notified that they will no longer be part of Trezor’s authorized sellers from 1st January. In addition, affected resellers were also meant to have their shipments stopped.

To the resellers who helped build Trezor: thank you, and I’m sorry 💔 https://t.co/RK7KBJOshp

— Danny (@Dantoshi) October 13, 2026

Trezor thanked its long-term distribution partners in order to extend access to its wallets, and noted that the new policy applies to companies working with the brand for many years.

Read More: Bits of Gold Breach May Expose 200,000 Crypto Users, But Funds Remain Safe Online

Trezor Says No Devices Have Been Compromised

One clear point that was set is that there is no evidence of Trezor hardware wallets being compromised.

The difference is significant, since the resellers belong to a report in which competitor hardware wallet provider Ledger is involved with an illegal hardware installation in at least one wallet.

They reported that it was not a typical attack regarding the firmware modification. Malicious hardware was made so as to collect confidential information for the purpose of recovery, and send it outside of the device.

Existing set-up on Trezor is designed to detect tampering, including counterfeiting, and firmware alteration, but a hardware tampering is a new form of a supply-chain threat.

Hardware Wallet Security Moves Beyond Firmware

The incident marks the scope of a problem afflicting self-custody users in general. Even though hardware wallets have secure, offline characteristics, their security can be influenced by how they move from manufacturer to the customer.

A physically tampered with device could outsmart a device that protects primarily against changes in the instruction set software or the firmware. That’s why, instead of making any announcement regarding the wallets, Trezor is putting more focus on reseller supervision.

Read More: Bitget Halts Withdrawals After $351.6M Hot Wallet Incident Hits Crypto Exchange

Users Urged to Check Where Their Wallet Comes From

Trezor has recommended its users to buy devices from the company if at all possible and ensure the products are intact. Users with larger crypto portfolios are further presented with multisignature setups as an option by the firm.

In the case of multisig, multiple keys are needed to validate a deal, which means that in the event of a compromised device, it will be unable to move funds alone. The reseller reduction, therefore, is a security measure for the supply chain and not a reaction to a confirmed hack on Trezor.

title: USDC Network Fees in 2026: Ethereum vs Solana vs Other Chains, Priced to the Cent
summary: Ask three people what it costs to send USDC and you will get three answers. One says five dollars. One says a fraction of a cent. The third says it depends. The third person is right, and the reason is more interesting than it sounds.
content:
Skip to content

Ask three people what it costs to send USDC and you will get three answers. One says five dollars. One says a fraction of a cent. The third says it depends. The third person is right, and the reason is more interesting than it sounds.

A USDC balance is the same dollar on every chain Circle issues it on. Moving it is not the same price. In October 2026 the spread between the cheapest and the most expensive way to send $25 runs from well under a cent to a fifth of the deposit, and most of that gap has little to do with blockchain gas. This piece prices each network, shows where the money actually goes, and works out what a month of small transfers costs on each route.

Three charges hide inside one “network fee”

Every USDC transfer can carry up to three costs. The first is gas, paid to the network in its native coin: ETH on Ethereum and its rollups, SOL on Solana, POL on Polygon. The second is the platform fee charged by whatever sends the coin. Exchanges usually take a flat amount per withdrawal, and they set it, not the chain. The third is setup, either a one-time account charge on some chains or a bridge fee when the coin has to change networks first.

Wallet screens tend to show only the first. Exchange screens tend to show only the second. The total is what leaves your balance, and that is the number worth comparing.

Ethereum mainnet: cheap gas, expensive habits

Ethereum earned its reputation in 2021, when gas above 100 gwei turned a stablecoin transfer into a ten-dollar errand. That is not 2026. Average gas has sat well under 1 gwei for most of this year, around 0.1 gwei by mid-2026 on Spark’s tracking.

The math is short. A USDC transfer burns roughly 45,000 units of gas, closer to 65,000 when the receiving address has never held USDC. With ETH near $2,700 in early October:

  • At 0.1 gwei: about 1 to 2 cents
  • At 1 gwei: about 12 to 18 cents
  • At 10 gwei: about $1.22 to $1.76
  • At 40 gwei, a busy day by current standards: about $4.86 to $7.02

So why do comparison guides still quote $2 to $5 for Ethereum? Because that is close to what exchanges charge. One of the largest venues lists a $5 USDC withdrawal on Ethereum against $0.80 on Solana. Another charges $4 on Ethereum and $1 on most other networks. Those fees did not fall when gas did.

For usd coin gambling on a small bankroll, that distinction decides everything. Send from a self-custody wallet and Ethereum costs pocket change most days. Send straight from an exchange and the same chain can eat 20% of a $25 deposit.

Solana: a fraction of a cent, plus a one-time charge

Solana prices transactions another way. Each signature carries a fixed base fee of 5,000 lamports, or 0.000005 SOL, with an optional priority tip on top. With SOL around $121 on October 6, that is about six hundredths of a cent per transfer.

There is one wrinkle. Solana keeps token balances in separate accounts, and a wallet that has never held USDC needs one created before it can receive any. Creating it locks up about 0.00204 SOL as rent, roughly 25 cents today. The sender usually pays it, once. Close the account later and that deposit comes back.

Settlement is quick. Transfers confirm in well under a second and finalize in about 13 seconds.Solana also holds the second largest pool of native USDC, about $8.6 billion against Ethereum’s $51 billion as of April 2026, per Circle’s transparency figures. Depth matters because it decides where exchanges and wallets route USDC by default.

Base, Arbitrum, Polygon and the low-cost middle

Between those two sits a crowd of networks that settle USDC for a cent or two. Eco’s May 2026 survey puts typical transfer costs at:

  • Base: about $0.01
  • Polygon PoS: about $0.01
  • Avalanche: about $0.01
  • Optimism: about $0.02
  • Arbitrum One: about $0.05
  • Stellar: about $0.00001

Base, Arbitrum and Optimism are rollups. They borrow Ethereum’s security by posting batches back to the main chain, which is why a Base transfer looks done in about two seconds but only becomes final at the Ethereum level after roughly 15 minutes. For a deposit that gap rarely matters. For larger sums, it is why some platforms wait longer before crediting rollup transfers.

Exchange fees still apply here. A flat $1 withdrawal on Polygon or Arbitrum is a hundred times the gas, or twenty.

What a month of $25 deposits actually costs

Per-transfer comparisons hide the part that hurts: repetition. Take a player who tops up a usdc casino balance with eight $25 deposits over a month, $200 in all.

  • Exchange withdrawal on Ethereum at $5: $40, or 20% of the money moved
  • Exchange withdrawal on a rollup at $1: $8, or 4%
  • Exchange withdrawal on Solana at $0.80: $6.40, or 3.2%
  • Self-custody wallet on Ethereum at 1 gwei: about $1.40, or 0.7%
  • Self-custody wallet on Arbitrum: about 40 cents
  • Self-custody wallet on Base: about 8 cents
  • Self-custody wallet on Solana: under a cent, plus 25 cents once if the receiving account is new

Now set that against the games. Wager the whole $200 once on titles returning 98% and the expected cost of play is $4. The first route on that list costs ten times the house edge before a single bet is placed. The last costs nothing worth counting.

There is a fix simpler than switching chains. Batch. One $200 deposit on the priciest exchange route costs $5, or 2.5%. Eight small ones cost 20%.

Moving USDC between chains without a wrapped token

Sometimes the coin is simply on the wrong network. The clean route is Circle’s Cross-Chain Transfer Protocol, which burns USDC on one chain and mints native USDC on the other instead of handing over a wrapped IOU. CCTP V2 charges no protocol fee; you pay gas at both ends. Its standard lane takes 13 to 19 minutes, set by the source chain’s finality. A Fast Transfer lane finishes in about 20 seconds.

The source chain still writes the bill. Moving USDC from Ethereum to Solana runs roughly $3 to $6 in Eco’s estimate, nearly all of it on the Ethereum side.

Third-party bridges are easier to find and sometimes cheaper between rollups, often 0.10% to 0.20% on a $1,000 transfer. The catch is what arrives. A wrapped or bridged token is not always accepted where native USDC is, and that mismatch is how deposits go missing.

Tron and the networks USDC has left

Plenty of wallets still offer a USDC option on Tron. Treat it as legacy. Circle stopped minting USDC on Tron in February 2024 and ended transfer support for its business customers in February 2025, citing its risk framework. Older tokens still exist, liquidity has thinned, and a platform that takes USDC elsewhere may not credit a Tron transfer at all. Tron is the cheap home of USDT, not USDC. Confusing the two is common and expensive.

The same rule covers every chain in this piece. You must send on a network the destination accepts. A USDC transfer to the right address on the wrong chain is not delayed. It is usually gone, and no fee saving is worth that.

Picking a network before you send

A short checklist covers most of it:

  • Check which networks the receiving platform supports, on its deposit screen rather than an old help article.
  • Compare the full cost: gas, the sender’s withdrawal fee and any account setup.
  • Use self-custody or a fee-free route for small, frequent transfers.
  • Batch wherever the fee is flat.
  • Send a small test amount the first time you use a new route.

Gambling sites show why step one matters. The Jacks Club USDC casino page, for example, says USDC covers deposits, play and withdrawals across the site, that deposits credit once the network confirms them, and that supported networks and minimums are listed on the deposit screen rather than fixed in the page copy. That is the right instinct. Network support changes faster than marketing text does.

Before any coin moves, check that online gambling is legal where you live and that the site accepts players from your country. Then do the arithmetic. Fees are the cost of getting a dollar to the table; the house edge is the cost of playing it. Only one of those is fully in your hands, and on most routes in 2026 it can be pushed close to zero.

title: Bitcoin (BTC) Price Prediction: Glassnode Signals Potential Price Floor Near $80K as Sellers Capitulate
summary: Bitcoin’s latest wave of loss-selling near $80,000 may indicate that selling pressure is approaching exhaustion, according to on-chain data from Glassnode.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: BTC

Bitcoin’s latest wave of loss-selling near $80,000 may indicate that selling pressure is approaching exhaustion, according to on-chain data from Glassnode.

Similar spikes in Bitcoin’s realized losses preceded local price bottoms in August and September, raising the possibility that the $80,000 region could provide near-term support for BTC.

However, the Bitcoin price outlook remains uncertain. Technical resistance near $83,000, continued spot Bitcoin ETF outflows, and concentrated liquidation levels around $80,600 and $82,300 suggest that BTC could face further volatility before establishing a clearer direction.

Glassnode Identifies Signs of Seller Capitulation

Glassnode reported another episode of Bitcoin seller capitulation on October 15, 2026, as BTC traded near the $80,000 region. Capitulation occurs when investors sell their holdings at a loss, often during periods of heightened uncertainty or declining prices.

Glassnode reports renewed Bitcoin seller capitulation on October 15, with realized loss spikes coinciding with local price bottoms in August and September 2026. Source: Glassnode via X

In its October 16 report, Glassnode noted that previous bursts of realized losses in early August, mid-August, and September coincided with local market bottoms. The latest episode follows a similar pattern, although the historical relationship does not guarantee another recovery.

Realized losses measure the value investors give up when they sell Bitcoin below the price at which they acquired it. A sharp increase in this metric can indicate that holders are exiting positions under pressure rather than waiting for a rebound.

Glassnode’s latest analysis also points to a decline in loss-taking among long-term holders. In its October 14 report, Boxed In, the analytics firm said long-term holder realized losses had fallen approximately 85% from their August 12 peak. The report also noted that holders realizing profits were increasingly outweighing those selling at a loss.

These developments provide a potentially constructive signal for the BTC price. When forced or emotionally driven selling subsides, the market may require less immediate buying demand to stabilize. Nevertheless, capitulation alone cannot confirm that a durable bottom has formed.

Bitcoin Price Prediction: $80K Support Faces a Critical Test

Bitcoin was trading around $82,000–$83,000 in the October 15–16 reporting period after briefly falling below $80,000 earlier in the month. The recovery places BTC above the psychologically important $80,000 level, but the market still needs to overcome nearby resistance.

Bitcoin (BTC) price chart. Source: Brave New Coin

Glassnode identified the U.S. spot Bitcoin ETF cost basis near $81,500 as an important support reference. This represents the average acquisition price of Bitcoin held by U.S. spot ETFs. According to the firm’s October 14 analysis, BTC dipped below this level on October 8 and October 13 but closed both sessions above it.

The firm warned that a daily close below the ETF cost basis could weaken the nearest on-chain support. Its report also identified substantial bids around $80,000 on Binance, creating another level to watch if selling pressure returns.

Meanwhile, a separate technical analysis published on TradingView by Virupandey81 identifies $79,821 as a key downside threshold. The chart places the initial positional-long reference at $81,263 and calls for confirmation before adding exposure above $83,014.

Bitcoin climbed from around $75,000 to $87,000 before correcting, recovering toward its previous high, and declining again, forming overlapping harmonic patterns. Source: Virupandey81 on TradingView

If Bitcoin holds above support and clears the $83,014 confirmation level, the chart identifies $87,233 as the first upside objective, followed by a projected extension near $91,754. These are technical targets rather than confirmed forecasts, and reaching them would require BTC to overcome intervening resistance.

A sustained move below $79,821 would weaken that bullish setup. The same chart identifies lower projected levels near $77,839 and $76,377, which could become relevant if the breakdown continues. Neither level guarantees a reversal.

The distinction is important for any Bitcoin price prediction: a potential support zone becomes more convincing when price repeatedly holds above it, while a decisive breakdown can invalidate an otherwise constructive setup.

Bitcoin Liquidation Heatmap Highlights $82.3K and $80.6K

Bitcoin’s derivatives market provides another indication of where short-term volatility could develop. CoinGlass shared a 48-hour liquidation heatmap showing concentrated leveraged positions around $82,300 and $80,600.

Bitcoin’s 48-hour liquidation heatmap shows concentrated high-leverage liquidation clusters around $82,300 and $80,600. Source: CoinGlass via X 

The upper zone near $82,300 represents a nearby cluster of potential liquidations, while the lower region around $80,600 contains another concentration of leveraged exposure. As BTC approaches these levels, forced position closures could amplify price movements.

Liquidation heatmaps estimate where leveraged positions may be vulnerable to forced closure. They do not show guaranteed buying or selling orders, and the displayed clusters can change as traders adjust their positions.

A move above $82,300 could trigger liquidations among traders positioned for further declines, potentially adding momentum to an upward move. Conversely, a drop toward $80,600 could put leveraged long positions under pressure, increasing the risk of a faster decline.

These levels also sit close to the broader support region highlighted by Glassnode. Their proximity makes the $80,000–$82,300 range particularly relevant to the near-term Bitcoin price forecast.

However, liquidation activity should be assessed alongside spot-market demand, trading volume and ETF flows. A temporary price spike caused by forced closures does not necessarily establish a lasting trend.

Bitcoin ETF Outflows Add Pressure to the Price Outlook

Despite the potential support signals from on-chain data, institutional investment flows remain a concern. U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded approximately $228.6 million in net outflows during the five trading sessions ending October 16, according to reported fund-flow data. Month-to-date net outflows reached roughly $615 million to $618 million.

BlackRock reportedly sold $570 million in Bitcoin as bearish forecasts warned of a potential drop to $75,000 after a brief rebound. Source: @Danny_Crypton via X

BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) accounted for approximately $165 million in weekly outflows, including about $71.8 million on October 16. Fidelity’s Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund also recorded outflows during the period.

These figures indicate that investors withdrew more money from the funds than they added during the measured period. However, they do not establish that BlackRock independently sold $570 million in Bitcoin on the open market, as claimed in a post by @Danny_Crypton on X.

ETF outflows reflect net investor redemptions and fund activity; they should not automatically be interpreted as evidence that an asset manager is deliberately pushing Bitcoin prices lower. The distinction matters when evaluating claims about institutional selling and the risk of a Bitcoin crash.

Continued redemptions could still weaken a source of market demand, particularly if they coincide with broader risk aversion. Glassnode’s October 14 report similarly noted that spot Bitcoin ETFs had returned to net selling after inflows in late September failed to persist.

The combination of ETF outflows and declining realized losses presents a mixed picture. Selling pressure among existing holders may be easing, but fresh investment demand has not yet provided a clear signal of sustained recovery.

What Comes Next for Bitcoin Price?

Bitcoin’s next move will likely depend on whether buyers can defend the $80,000 region while absorbing selling pressure and overcoming nearby resistance.

The bullish scenario gains support if BTC maintains the area around the $81,500 ETF cost basis, holds above the $80,000–$80,600 support zone, and moves through $83,014. Under the TradingView chart’s projections, $87,233 would be the first upside target, with $91,754 representing a more distant objective.

The bearish scenario becomes more relevant if Bitcoin loses the $79,821 technical threshold and fails to recover it. In that case, the projected levels around $77,839 and $76,377 would become areas to monitor, while liquidation activity could accelerate the decline.

Glassnode’s capitulation data offers evidence that some selling pressure may be reaching an extreme, but it is only one part of the market picture. ETF flows, liquidity conditions, spot demand, and price behavior around support will help determine whether the latest loss-selling episode marks a local floor or merely another pause in Bitcoin’s decline.

For now, the $80,000 region remains a key reference point in the Bitcoin price prediction. A sustained recovery would strengthen the case for higher targets, while a decisive breakdown would challenge the emerging stabilization signal.

title: Hedera (HBAR) Price Analysis as Long-Term Compression Tests Support
summary: The price of Hedera (HBAR) is returning to $0.08275, a major technical support level, amid bearish pressure.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: HBAR

The price of Hedera (HBAR) is returning to $0.08275, a major technical support level, amid bearish pressure.

The monthly chart of the instrument has a long-term pattern of a triangle, which may form the next significant price action. On the 4-hour time frame, HBAR has broken above its October highs, signaling a momentum decline.

The major issue is whether buyers can justify the existing support level and hold the market. If the sustained recovery continues, the resistance could be seen in the descent, and if the breakdown occurs, the lower levels near $0.071 could be seen.

HBAR Faces Selling Pressure Below $0.092

According to BraveNewCoin market data, HBAR is currently trading at $0.08275, falling by 2.61% in the last 24 hours. The token’s price range in the past 24 hours is 0.08207-0.08710. The value of its market capitalization is $3.64 billion, and the trading volume is $104.75 million.

On the other hand, the 4-hour chart for HBAR indicates that the token is currently trading at $0.08234 on October 17, 2026. The price is out of the trendline chart and sitting near $0.09212. with a falling trendline. This is now the level that is an upper limit for recovery, but buyers need to muster a powerful response to test it.

Four-Hour Chart Signals Further Downside Risk

On the 4-hour chart, HBAR is consolidating its gains and heading back to the $0.12 level from its highs seen in late September. The ongoing sell-off has driven the token near the bottom of its Bollinger Bands. The bottom of its lower band is at $0.07103, and the top of its upper band is at $0.11322.

HBAR is trading at $0.09212, which is close to the middle line of the chart’s trend indicator. Source: TradingView

This formation indicates that the sellers are still holding the upper hand in the recent price trend. But a turn up from below $0.09212 would be better for the near term and could create resistance at $0.10.

Monthly Triangle Keeps the $0.57 Level in Focus

HBAR continues to trade inside of a long-term triangle pattern, as seen on the monthly chart shared on X. Both rising support and descending resistance continue to the lows from 2020 and 2021 highs, respectively. The price has been compressed between these two trending lines over the past few years, hence the pattern.

The chart below shows a possible scenario for a breakout where HBAR may move back toward $0.57 in the future. Source: Giannis Via X

This level corresponds to the peak from the provided market data that occurred in the past. However, this is a conditional projection, and the price hasn’t confirmed a breakout above the descending resistance.

Support and Resistance Levels to Watch

The immediate support level is around $0.0820, the daily low for HBAR. If the price stays below this level for an extended period, it may reach the lower Bollinger Band around $0.07103. Traders can also watch to see whether buyers support the wider uptrend on the monthly chart.

The good news is that HBAR will need to rally to $0.09212 to threaten its downtrending near-term condition. Further resistance could emerge around $0.10 and the recent peak above $0.12. A close-out above the monthly triangle’s resistance would support the big-time recovery outlook.
